edges.description: Bacillemia from the pulmonary infection implants bacilli in the epididymis.
The same bacillemia seeds the kidneys and prostate, giving urinary tract and prostatic tuberculosis.
Healed implantation foci enter a latent phase from which they later reactivate.
edges.target: Reactivation of a Latent Epididymal Focus

edges.description: Reactivated bacilli drive active caseating granulomatous inflammation, starting in the tail of the epididymis.
edges.source: Reactivation of a Latent Epididymal Focus

edges.description: Bacilli from infected urine and prostate pass along the ejaculatory ducts and vas deferens to the epididymis.
edges.target: Retrograde Canalicular Spread to the Epididymis

edges.description: Urinary tract tuberculosis produces pyuria, which is found in a minority of patients with tuberculous epididymo-orchitis.
Urinary tract tuberculosis produces microscopic hematuria in some patients.
Bacilli arriving by the canalicular route establish granulomatous epididymitis in the globus minor.
edges.source: Retrograde Canalicular Spread to the Epididymis

edges.description: The enlarging granulomatous lesion is felt as a firm, often nodular or beaded swelling of the epididymis.
Epididymal inflammation causes scrotal pain in a large minority of patients; many swellings are painless.
The granulomatous lesion is seen histologically as caseating granulomatous inflammation.
Active tuberculous inflammation is accompanied by fever in some patients.
Active tuberculous inflammation is accompanied by weight loss in a minority of patients.
Untreated disease extends from the epididymis into the testis and scrotal tissues.
edges.target: Contiguous Extension to the Testis and Scrotal Wall

edges.description: Granulomatous masses, and later fibrosis and scarring, block the lumen of the epididymis and vas deferens.
edges.target: Epididymal and Vasal Obstruction and Fibrosis

edges.description: Extension into the testis gives tuberculous epididymo-orchitis.
edges.source: Contiguous Extension to the Testis and Scrotal Wall

edges.description: Liquefied caseous material forms a cold abscess in the epididymis or scrotum.
edges.source: Contiguous Extension to the Testis and Scrotal Wall

edges.description: Caseous lesions adherent to the scrotum ulcerate through the skin as discharging sinuses.

edges.description: Inflammation reaching the tunica vaginalis produces a reactive hydrocele.

nodes.description: Standard six-month antituberculous chemotherapy, four drugs in the intensive phase (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) and isoniazid with rifampicin in the continuation phase, is first-line for all genital tuberculosis.

evidence.reference_title: Genital tuberculosis: current status of diagnosis and management.
evidence.snippet: Anti-tubercular chemotherapy is the first line of management for all forms of genital Tb and a 6 months course is the standard of care.

evidence.reference_title: Genital tuberculosis: current status of diagnosis and management.
evidence.snippet: Most patients are started with four drugs in the first two months ‘the intensive phase’ of the regimen (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol) and are then shifted to two drugs in the ‘continuation phase’ (rifampicin and isoniazid)

nodes.description: Because obstruction is often at several levels and not reconstructable, most men with tuberculous obstructive azoospermia need in-vitro fertilisation or intracytoplasmic sperm injection, using epididymal or testicular sperm.

evidence.reference_title: Genital tuberculosis: current status of diagnosis and management.
evidence.snippet: Thus, most patients with tuberculous infertility will need assisted reproduction, and in-vitro fertilization or intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection is usually feasible

nodes.description: Epithelioid macrophages, Langhans giant cells and lymphocytes form granulomas around foci of caseous necrosis, producing caseous nodules that enlarge and bead the epididymis.

nodes.description: The testis, protected from bloodborne spread by the blood-testis barrier, is involved by direct extension from the epididymis. Caseous lesions can adhere to the scrotum, form a cold abscess and ulcerate through the skin as sinus tracts.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of epididymal tuberculosis: a review of 47 cases.
evidence.snippet: The pathological features of epididymal tuberculosis are extensive tissue destruction and fibrosis, eventually leading to destruction of the epididymis and surrounding genital tissues and organs and complications such as infertility and other serious effects on male reproductive system function.

nodes.description: Surgical excision of the epididymis, or of the epididymis and testis when the testis is involved, combined with chemotherapy before and after surgery. Chinese surgical series use it routinely for advanced or complicated disease (abscess, sinus, testicular involvement) and when a tumour cannot be excluded; a review notes that most patients respond to chemotherapy alone and that surgery is now rarely needed for diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of tuberculous epididymo-orchitis: a retrospective study of 81 cases with long-term follow-up.
evidence.snippet: Given TB of the testis is always secondary to infection of the epididymis, epididymectomy (33.3%) and epididymo-orchidectomy (64.2%) were the main surgical procedure for TBEO in our study.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of epididymal tuberculosis: a review of 47 cases.
